description: Governed vectors of the acse-tenant module (spec 02e sections 3 and 4, Amendments 2 to 4 and 6; ledger 02e sections 10.2a, 10.3, 10.10, 11.0b and 12.8). Every store path the module creates or grants, and the shape and exact bytes of every file it generates, for each case's tenant.yaml. Produced by tools/render_vectors.py; tests/*.tftest.hcl hold the module equal to it. Synthetic values.

secret_rules.name: acse/<tenant>/<path> (no leading slash)
secret_rules.created_by: acse-tenant: the secret container only. No version is ever written or read by Terraform; a secret with no version is the placeholder (reported missing until the value is put in).
secret_rules.kms: kms_key_arn when set, else the AWS-managed aws/secretsmanager key

parameter_rules.name: /acse/<tenant>/<path> (leading slash: SSM requires one for a name that contains '/')
parameter_rules.type: String, data_type text, tier Advanced (8 KB) for every index and part; more than 64 parts refuses to plan

parameters.when: the section is present in tenant.yaml; settings/naming always ({} when naming is absent)
parameters.written_by: acse-tenant (the setup apply) only, index last
parameters.value: always a settings-index-1.0 document (DEC-6): jsonencode of {schema, section, commit, sha256, bytes, parts, inline}, keys sorted; inline (parts 0) when that document is <= 8192 bytes, else parts n and no inline. payload = the tenant.yaml section exactly as written (not normalised), as Terraform jsonencode renders it: keys sorted, no whitespace, '<' '>' '&' escaped as \u003c \u003e \u0026; sha256 and bytes are over the payload's UTF-8 bytes; commit is the setup commit applied

parameters.written_by: acse-tenant, before the index; stale parts destroyed after it
parameters.value: the payload's i-th slice, at most 7168 bytes, cut by characters (7168 per part for an ASCII payload, 1792 otherwise), so no UTF-8 sequence is split; readers concatenate in order and check bytes and sha256

parameters.written_by: keygen only; acse-tenant neither creates nor writes it
parameters.value: {key_id, public_key_pem, sha256, next:{key_id, public_key_pem, sha256}} (keygen's shape)

saas.when: saas_publish_role_arn is set (spec 02e Amendment 6 section A; ledger 02e section 12.8, SA-1 to SA-7)
saas.cloud: tenant.yaml cloud.* names InitValue's runtime account and region, which hold the runtime, the namespace and the publish role (SA-4); the publish role must be in cloud.account
saas.skipped: the namespace (secret containers and parameters as resources), the GitHub OIDC provider, and the promoter role (SA-6): InitValue's pipeline creates them
saas.kept: the rulesets, the generated files, the setup apply environment and OIDC subject template, and the setup roles when setup_credential_store is aws (in the customer's own account, the account of setup_credential_secret_arn)
saas.publish: write-only, on apply only, by provisioners that call scripts/saas-publish.sh as the publish role: PutParameter (String, text, Advanced, overwrite) for each part then the index of every section on every apply; DeleteParameter for a part or index that leaves the configuration (one terraform_data slot per parameter, deleted on destroy); PutSecretValue on github/read/private-key and github/change/private-key when saas_app_keys_version changes. State holds {commit, sha256, parts} per section and parameter names, never a value

publish_role.trust: the apply job's SC-1 subject, through cloud.account's GitHub OIDC provider, aud sts.amazonaws.com, StringEquals
grants: kms:GenerateDataKey via secretsmanager.<region>.amazonaws.com, only when kms_key_arn is set
publish_role.created_by: InitValue's infrastructure pipeline, per tenant (SA-2); the module only renders publish_policy and publish_trust_policy

promoter_role.when: repositories.outbox is set and manage_promoter_role is true
promoter_role.arn: cloud.workflow_role exactly (its account must be cloud.account)
grants: kms:Decrypt on kms_key_arn with kms:ViaService secretsmanager.<region>.amazonaws.com, only when kms_key_arn is set

setup_roles.when: setup_credential_store is aws and setup_credential_secret_arn is set (DEC-20); with setup_credential_store gcp there are no AWS roles, only the environment, the subject template and the three subjects (setup_oidc_subjects), which modules/gcp-setup-credential binds (SA-5)
setup_roles.subject_template: the setup repository's OIDC subject template is always include_claim_keys [repo, context, job_workflow_ref] (SC-1); <segment> is setup_oidc_subject_repo, owner/name or owner@id/name@id (immutable format)

apply.name: acse-setup-apply (setup_apply_role_name)
apply.reads: the setup credential secret (customer-named, outside acse/<tenant>/); its resource policy denies GetSecretValue to every other principal but setup_credential_extra_reader_arns

plan.name: acse-setup-plan (setup_plan_role_name)
plan.operator: StringEquals (push-only is the template's job condition: AWS cannot match event_name)
plan.reads: only the read-only App's key (setup_plan_credential_secret_arn, customer-named, outside acse/<tenant>/); its resource policy denies every other principal

check.name: acse-setup-check (setup_check_role_name)
check.operator: StringLike (the pull request number only; must be tested on a real organization, fails closed)
check.reads: never the setup credential, and no GitHub credential at all (SC-5): the pull request plans the cloud side only

setup_roles.environment: acse-setup-apply in the setup repository: deployable from the default branch only, can_admins_bypass false, prevent_self_review true, at least one required reviewer

rulesets.name: acse-change-only-on-acse-branches
rulesets.bypass_actors: RepositoryRole 4 (write), 2 (maintain), 5 (admin); Integration per ruleset_bypass_integration_ids; DeployKey unless ruleset_bypass_deploy_keys is false; all bypass_mode always; never ACSE Change

rulesets.name: acse-change-no-force-push
rulesets.not_restricted: deletion (the deep test deletes {b}/connectivity-test), creation, update
rulesets.bypass_actors: the same list as the branch ruleset; never ACSE Change
rulesets.enforcement: the same as the branch ruleset; LR-6's force_push_blocked passes only when active

rulesets.name: acse-change-no-tags
rulesets.bypass_actors: the same list as the branch ruleset
rulesets.enforcement: the same as the branch ruleset

generated_file_rules.bytes: two-space indent, members in schema order, values as Terraform jsonencode renders them, one trailing line feed
generated_file_rules.generated_from: repository = repositories.setup; commit = the setup commit at which the rest of the file last changed (latched; not rewritten when only the commit changes); tenant_yaml_sha256 = sha256 over the bytes of config/tenant.yaml at that commit
generated_file_rules.compared: with generated_from excluded, as the runtime's drift check compares
generated_file_rules.pull_request_branch: setup-apply/acse-gate-config-<12 hex> or setup-apply/acse-promote-config-<12 hex>: the first 12 hex of sha256 over the payload (the file without generated_from) as jsonencode renders it

generated_files.when: gate.audience and gate.report_url are both set
generated_files.members: gate_config_format_version, tenant, audience, report_url, generated_from{repository, commit, tenant_yaml_sha256}
promoter_config_format_version, tenant, cloud{provider, region, workflow_role, namespace}, generated_from{repository, commit, tenant_yaml_sha256}
